extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, litigators, and judges handling equitable remedies for patent infringement
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and drafting guidance for bills seeking injunctions in patent litigation and the equitable principles courts apply in granting, continuing, or dissolving injunctions. Covers who may be parties, required allegations and affidavits, procedural prerequisites, and the discretionary factors courts weigh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parties entitled to relief in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties entitled to relief in equity against the infringement of a patent are, first, the party or parties interested in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedy in equity is given to protect a legal right; the statute gives a right of action to the person(s) interested, whether as patentee, assignees, or grantees of the exclusive right for a particular district; any person holding legal title or the right to bring an action may bring a bill for an injunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee standing and recording requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the assignee has the whole interest, he may sue alone; but if he has less than the whole interest, he must join the patentee. If the assignment has not been recorded, the assignee is not substituted to the right and responsibility of the patentee so as to maintain any suit at law or in equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An unrecorded assignment may be a fatal defect on the face of the bill. Where a joint suit is brought and the patentee files a disclaimer not joined by the assignee, the disclaimer cannot operate for complainants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee for particular district may sue at law; equity joinder
rubrics_metrics.description: The grantee of the exclusive right for a particular district may bring an action at law within his own district in his own name; in equity the patentee may be joined with such assignee because certain incidents of the patentee's interest remain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A grantee limited to using a specified number of machines or a territory may maintain a law action in his district; in equity the patentee is a proper party where the assignee's interest is limited and the patentee retains rights (e.g., ability to license further use for consideration).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendants must be related in title or conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Different persons who have infringed a patent independently of each other cannot be made defendants in the same bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joinder of defendants is restricted; the bill should sue the proper parties according to their relation to the alleged infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required recitals in a bill for an injunction (letters-patent and title)
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill should recite the application for the letters-patent by the inventor, compliance with prerequisites, the issue of the letters, giving the title as contained in them, verbatim, their attestation by proper officers, and their delivery to the patentee; profert of the letters should be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary to set forth the description of the invention in the specification. When the bill is brought on assignee title or when patent has been renewed/extended/amended, those facts should be set forth to show present state of title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegation of use and exclusive possession
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary to state that the plaintiff, after issuing of the patent, put his invention into use, and is, at the time of filing the bill, in the exclusive possession of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations of actual use/exclusive possession support requests for equitable relief and can be decisive in whether equity will act before a law trial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of the infringement and related history
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill should state the infringement complained of, whether it has been actually committed or is threatened; and if the right has been previously established by an action at law or an injunction obtained, that fact should be set forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These averments should typically be followed by alleging requests to the defendant to desist and to account, and allegations of combination or conspiracy if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prayer and remedies to include in the bill
rubrics_metrics.description: The prayer of the bill is for a discovery upon oath and particular answers to interrogatories; for a general answer; for decree that the defendant account for and pay over gains and profits; for an injunction to restrain further use; to compel delivery or destruction of machines or things made; and for further relief, closing with a writ of injunction and subpoena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interrogatories should be pointed at material averments. The bill should be sworn to by the usual affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit requirement accompanying application
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain an injunction, the plaintiff must accompany his application with an affidavit that he then believes himself to be the original and first inventor of the thing patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This special affidavit addresses the possibility that circumstances or new information could have convinced the patentee he was mistaken at the time of patenting; it is usual practice on moving for an injunction before answer to read such affidavit and others to the same effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement in U.S. courts for injunction motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice that an injunction is to be applied for must be served on the defendant; no injunction, temporary or final, can be granted without reasonable previous notice to the adverse party or his attorneys of the time and place of moving for the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice, injunctions in U.S. patent cases are not granted on ex parte applications though they may be granted on filing the bill and before answer if proper notice is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath omission is not fatal after hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The omission of the oath is not a ground for demurrer after a hearing and order to file evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such objection should be made by motion on the appearance of the respondents, when the oath will be directed unless good cause to the contrary be shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental bill when patent surrendered and renewed
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent is surrendered and renewed pending proceedings, a supplemental bill is necessary in order to continue the injunction as to the new patent; by supplemental bill the plaintiff may also bring in new parties and enlarge the charges of the original bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts will generally continue an injunction as to a new patent stated in a supplemental bill until hearing or further order where the commissioner has granted a new patent for the same invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court's discretionary courses on interlocutory injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon application for an interlocutory injunction the court may (1) grant the injunction simpliciter; (2) grant an injunction and at the same time direct the plaintiff to proceed to establish his title at law, suspending the injunction until the result of legal investigation; (3) retain the bill giving plaintiff opportunity to establish title at law; or (4) dismiss the bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Which course to take depends entirely on the discretion of the court according to the case made; great latitude is allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court's latitude at the hearing to grant injunction without law trial
rubrics_metrics.description: When the cause comes to a hearing the court has a large latitude and may, in rare cases, be of opinion that the injunction may properly be granted without recourse to a trial at law where conduct of parties, frame of pleadings, nature of patent right, and evidence combine to justify it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is 'unquestionably competent' if the judge's mind is satisfied that such course will do justice between the parties, although this is not often done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity will act without prior law trial where exclusive possession of some duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent has been granted and there has been an exclusive possession of some duration under it, the court will interpose its injunction without putting the party previously to establish the validity of his patent by an action at law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Lord Eldon's rule; the commissioner granting a subsequent patent with amended specification is prima facie evidence that the patents are for the same invention and will be accepted unless clear proof of fraud, excess of authority, or manifest discrepancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court will require law trial when patent is new or defects are glaring
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patent is 'but of yesterday' or defects in the patent or specification are so glaring that the court can entertain no doubt as to invalidity, the court will not act on presumed validity and will send the patentee to law to establish the validity before granting an injunction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reasonable doubt exists as to plaintiff's right or validity of patent, equity will require a trial at law (sometimes expedited) and may permit a return for an account if law trial is in plaintiff's favor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reluctance to grant injunction where accounting suffices or risk to defendant
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts of equity are loath to grant an injunction unless the plaintiff's right is very clear, especially in cases where an account will answer all reasonable purposes; they are unwilling to restrain a defendant who may have constructed a machine at great expense until a decision at law can be had.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vice-chancellors have considered it unusual to order indemnity/security for defendants; courts weigh hardship to defendants when deciding equitable relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner's grant as prima facie evidence (renewal/surrender context)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patentee has surrendered his original patent and taken out another one with an amended specification, the action of the commissioner in granting the subsequent patent is prima facie evidence that the two patents are for the same invention and can only be invalidated by clear proof of fraud, excess of authority, or manifest discrepancy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts generally will not re-examine the commissioner's decision except where the new patent on its face shows repugnancy or collusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bill quia timet and injunction as prima facie evidence of intended violation
rubrics_metrics.description: A bill will lie quia timet (for apprehended intention to violate) if the patent right is admitted or has been established upon well-grounded proof of an apprehended intention of the defendant to violate the patent right; an injunction already granted is prima facie evidence of intended violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equity may enjoin based on apprehended violations; affidavits and prior injunctions strengthen the prima facie case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant's later patent pleadings do not bind court to commissioner's interference procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the defendant, in his answer, does not impeach the validity of the complainant's patent but sets up a subsequent patent granted to himself and denies infringement, the court is not precluded by the commissioner's act in granting the subsequent patent without notice of interference to the prior patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commissioner's action is not conclusive against the prior patentee's legal remedies; the court may examine the legal rights notwithstanding the administrative proceedings.
